<reason>A won the central clash: whether culture-type benefits can be expressed as checkable role-specific reasons. A's recurring ju-jitsu — every concrete benefit B names (hallway questions, whiteboard fixes, juniors learning by proximity) is itself a writable, falsifiable reason — forced B onto a single defensive line (density can't be itemized), and A answered it with a coherent criterion (named mechanism + checkability) plus the function-level anchor answer. A answered both pressure questions directly under the required A1:/A2: labels, defused the toothless-or-paralyzing dilemma ("both horns concede the sentence can be written; honesty on the record disciplines without a referee"), and turned B's hospital example against it. A's critique of market discipline — a slow, garbled signal arriving only after the most mobile leave — was never rebutted; B just restated "let workers judge the bargain." B's density/commons argument and Q2 trap were the best original material in the debate, and the paperwork-vs-paralysis dilemma was crisply framed, but B repeated it across three speeches without resolving A's key distinction that the motion requires justification, not exemption. Both sides were epistemically clean, format-compliant, and rhetorically strong; A simply adapted and closed the clash better.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A's Rebuttal 1 pivot — "those are specific, articulable business reasons; so write them down" — converted B's best example into proof of the motion's feasibility and set the frame B spent the rest of the debate failing to escape; B's sharpest counter-thrust (Q2 and the density dilemma) was directly answered in A's A2 with the mechanism-plus-falsifiability criterion.</best_rebuttal>
